newsitem.title: UK: Pru to re-test sales force after SIB report.
newsitem.headline: Pru to re-test sales force after SIB report.

text.p: Britain's biggest life insurance group, Prudential Corp, said on Wednesday it is to re-test its entire direct sales force over the summer.

Confirming a report in the Financial Times newspaper, the company said the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) had ordered it to re-test more than 5,000 staff after the watchdog uncovered shortcomings in the Pru's training and compliance procedures.
A spokesman for the Pru said the basic problem was the way the sales force had been trained in the company's own products.
He said the Pru was taking the problem very seriously but declined to give out figures on how much the exercise was going to cost.
"There will be some costs but it's not going to be enormously disruptive," he said.

The latest critcisms come at a bad time for the Pru. It was named less than a month ago as being among the worst offenders in the pension mis-selling scandal that has dogged the industry in recent years.
And a draft SIB report leaked two weeks ago criticised the Pru for wrongly advising clients to put money into one of its most popular products, the Prudential Savings Account.
The re-testing will be completed by the end of September.

The Pru decided it needed to improve its compliance regime at the end of last year and has brought in accountants KPMG to look at procedures and the company said the process of improving compliance was already underway.
